summary: Usha R. Jain is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of California, Berkeley. She worked as an RDH at Dr Ritu Punia DMD in 2024 and was attested as Senior Lecturer Emerita at UC Berkeley in 2026.
Usharbudh Arya (1933–2015) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of London and held a post at the University of Minnesota from circa 1967 to 1973.
Uta Reinöhl is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She held a post at the University of Cologne in 2018 and became Chair of General Linguistics at the University of Freiburg in 2026.

Ute Hüsken is an Indologist and scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her doctorate under Heinz Bechert at Göttingen (~1991–1995), later teaching at Göttingen, Heidelberg University (2003–2008, 2017), and the University of Oslo (2007–2017).

Ute Wallenböck, a scholar of Sinology and Tibetology, studied at the University of Vienna and Sigmund Freud University Vienna. Her posts include Masaryk University (2019–2024), Palacký University Olomouc (2019–2022), and the University of Bonn (2024).

Uto von Melzer (1881–1961) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Graz (PhD 1919–1923) under Johann Kirste, Rudolf Meringer, and Hans Reichelt.

Utz Podzeit (1942–2022) was an Indologist who completed his Dr. phil. at the University of Vienna (1965–1972). He served as Universitätsdozent at Vienna starting in 1969 and conducted research at the University of Madras (1972–1974).
V. Kameswari is an Indologist affiliated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, serving on the editorial committee (attested 2001) and as a supervisor/guide (attested 2026).
V. M. Subramanya Sharma is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as Assistant Professor at Osmania University from 2011 to 2022 and at the University of Delhi starting in 2022.

Vinayaka P. Bhatta is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. At Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, he served as head of the Sanskrit Dictionary Project (attested 2011) and Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary (attested 2026).
V. R. Srinivasan is an Indology and religious studies scholar attested in 2026 as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.

Indologist V. Raghavan (1908–1979) earned his Ph.D. at the University of Madras under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He worked at the University of Madras (1934–1968) and served as secretary of the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (~1944–1979).

V. W. Paranjpe (1887–1976) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi. He worked at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 1927) and later became Professor Emeritus at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.
Vaibhav Singh is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Reading in 2017 and held a post there attested in 2018.

Indologist Vairamuthu Kanagaraj studied at SASTRA and IIT Hyderabad. He held research positions at the National Institute of Indian Medical Heritage (2023–2025) and Jayadev Memorial Rashtrotthana Hospital (2025), and served as Teaching Assistant at IIT Hyderabad in 2026.

Valaiyattur Venkayya (1864–1912) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He served as Acting Government Epigraphist of Madras (~1903–1908) and Acting Government Epigraphist for the Archaeological Survey of India (1905).

Valdo H. Viglielmo (1926–2016) was a scholar of Japanology and philosophy. Educated at Harvard, Tokyo, and Gakushuin, he taught at Harvard, Princeton, and several universities in Japan before serving as Professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1965–2002).

Valentin Parisot (1800–1861) was a French Indologist and linguist educated at the École Normale Supérieure. He served as Professor of Foreign Literature at the universities of Rennes (1842–1847), Grenoble Alpes (1847–1853), and Douai (1854).

Valentin Trapp (1908–1993) was an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Munich (1930–1933). He also studied at Visva-Bharati and Banaras Hindu University, working under scholars including Hanns Oertel, Lucian Scherman, and Walther Wüst.

Valentina Stache-Rosen (1925–1980) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. under Ernst Waldschmidt at the University of Göttingen (1944–1954) and also studied at SOAS University of London and Deccan College.
